title: deps: update the shared Next.js lock to the patched 15.5 release

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

The root npm lock at main `d41ec9fcb796504d85f5a5247a5fdc9eb3e65de5` resolves `next@15.5.21`, shared by `site` and `gui/app`. GitHub reports two open critical dependency alerts affecting that version:

- [AVIF image-optimization advisory](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4), alert 107.
- [Windows-hosted server advisory](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36), alert 106.

Both publisher advisories identify `15.5.24` as the first patched release on the existing major line. This establishes an affected locked dependency; production endpoint exposure has not been established. Both app configurations use static export and unoptimized images, while development/CI also uses a Next server. Complete hosting, operating-system and runtime reachability were not audited, so the static configuration is not grounds to dismiss the alerts.

A bounded independent assessment by actual Claude Opus 5 recommends a prompt, narrow patch follow-up after the current #6478 implementation lane. Implement with GPT-6 Astra and obtain independent Opus review. Keep this separate from the query-budget fix.

Acceptance:

- Update the resolved Next version to the patched 15.5 line using the repository's supported npm version. Check all nested lock entries and verify both workspaces resolve the patched version. Record whether the declared minimums also move from `^15.5.21` to `^15.5.24`.
- Preserve existing overrides, static-export/image/base-path settings, webpack aliases and unrelated dependency floors; inspect any transitive lock churn. Do not perform a broad dependency upgrade.
- Verify reproducible install, supported Node/React compatibility, relevant site/GUI builds, lint and existing development-server/e2e checks. Investigate any visual regression; do not blindly update snapshots. Use normal protected CI and merge queue.
- Recheck the two alerts after the fix reaches main and confirm automatic resolution. Do not manually dismiss them. Revalidate current advisory/patch status before implementation.

Targeted open issue/PR searches found no existing Next patch or matching advisory follow-up. This tracks remediation and validation; it does not claim exploitation or a completed security audit.
